pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are characters and events in a text related to real life?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension
2. appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 4.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
This lesson teaches Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading for Grade 9 ENGLISH.

STUDY STEPS
1. answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading above.
2. Explain Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 4.2.1 Intensive Reading important for a Grade 9 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are characters and events in a text related to real life?
2. Why is note taking an important reading skill?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. answer direct and inferential questions for comprehension
2. appreciate the importance of intensive reading in lifelong learning

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
